_comment: Canonical reference for the vector_type and auth_mode values used in email_services.json and scenario_templates.json attack vectors. NOTE: vector_type is the technical channel of a vector (web_ui, smtp_server, network...) — NOT to be confused with a mail service's service_type (Email Delivery Service, Free Mail Provider, Shared Hosting). DOCUMENTATION ONLY: this file is not loaded at runtime — keep it in sync with the JSON that is (email_services.json, scenario_templates.json) and with models.AttackVector._AUTH_REQUIRED_MODES.

web_ui.description: Human-operated web interface used to compose or configure email delivery from a browser dashboard.

http_api.description: Programmatic email submission through the provider's HTTP/REST API (distinct from the human web_ui).

smtp_server.description: Email submission through the provider's SMTP endpoint (SMTP AUTH), or an unauthenticated SMTP relay.

local_script.description: Locally executed script submitting through the local MTA on shared hosting, without external SMTP auth. Examples: PHP mail() (most prevalent), sendmail wrapper, Python smtplib to localhost.

email_forwarding.description: Provider-side forwarding rule configured through an account or webmail interface.

network.description: Network-level interception/manipulation of the SMTP connection to the MX (MITM). Service authentication is not the relevant access mechanism.

credentials.description: Reusable account credentials, typically a username/email + password (web login or SMTP AUTH LOGIN/PLAIN). The exact SMTP mechanism is intentionally not fixed here.

api_key.description: Provider-issued API key/token used for SMTP AUTH (e.g. apikey:<key>) or the HTTP API.

app_password.description: Application-specific password generated when 2FA is active (Gmail, Yahoo, iCloud, AOL...).

oauth_token.description: Short-lived or refreshable OAuth access/refresh token authorizing web, API, or SMTP access (Gmail, Microsoft 365...).

trusted_local_submission.description: Submission authorized implicitly because it originates from a trusted local process or hosting account (PHP mail(), sendmail). Replaces the former 'local_mta' auth_mode.

none.description: The service accepts the operation without authentication — by design or by misconfiguration (e.g. open relay, no-policy direct spoof).

not_applicable.description: Authentication is not a relevant concept for this vector (e.g. network interception). Replaces the former null auth_mode.

Shared Hosting._note: api_key is possible (not typical) for providers exposing token-based SMTP relay (e.g. Infomaniak, some cPanel/Plesk setups).
